INFORMATION SYSTEMS

The term network in telecommunications is a broad term that could be referencing any of a number of communication activities such as cellular telephone networks, ISDN (integrated services digital network), LANs (local area network), WANs (wide area network), satellite networks, and so on...
DISCUSSION

Networks are most simply defined as an arrangement of electronic devices designed to communicate with one another. Not long ago, nearly all networks were connected to one another through a specialized system of cables, which were often complex and expensive...
Many networks employ a variety of mediums, typically fiber optics and radio frequency (RF). More recently, wireless networks have taken center stage in the world of telecommunication networks...
Point-To-Multi-Point Wireless Link With Antenna On Each Roof

Most all computer networks fall into one of three categories: LANs, WANs or MANs. The two most common are LANs and WANs. LAN is an acronym for Local Area Network and a WAN is Wide Area Network. Other ways of categorizing networks are whether they are public or private, broadcast or switched...

There was a time when a LAN or a WAN was easily defined and their differences easily distinguished. Presently, this is not the case, because the defining factors have evolved. During the 1980s, a LAN was normally restricted to a single structure or cluster of buildings where the LAN elements were not more than a hundred to a thousand feet apart.....

Since then, some LANs have come to encompass areas tens of miles wide. This would normally suggest a WAN, but other characteristics come into play. WANs are normally provided by a third party and are considered public networks (even though some of them aren't). That is, the service is provided to anyone willing to pay for it.....

A telephone network is a good example of a WAN. The Internet is also a WAN, although it has many characteristics that are unique. In contrast, LANs are normally privately owned, as those found in businesses, government offices, police departments, college campuses, and even some private residences. These LANs are for the use of specific individuals and not the public.....

Operational speeds and error rates can also be a defining characteristic. LANs normally operate in the kilobyte range with a very small error rate. WANs are normally operating in the megabyte range but have a considerably higher rate of errors...

This is because WANs are often required to operate in environments that are not necessarily conducive to error-free transmissions and must perform through multiple mediums in a variety of weather conditions...

While LANs and WANs may be the most common network types, there is yet another form called a MAN (Metropolitan Area Network). It would be far too easy to say that a MAN is a network that serves a metropolitan area; however, it would not necessarily be correct...
Which computer network is the least common?
A LAN is one of the two most common computer networks......

Suppose in Gotham City, USA, Wayne Corporation has three separate buildings in different parts of the city: engineering, production, and publications. All three departments have their own LAN. The Director of Operations decides that it would be advantageous for the people in production to have direct access to engineering, engineering to publications, etc...........................

Solution: connect the LANs together to make a MAN. After another brainstorming session, it is decided that the marketing department, located on the other side of the country, should have their LAN connected to the newly formed MAN, which results in a WAN. A MAN, then, can be thought of as two or more LANs connected together in a geographically restricted area...............

While enough confusion is generated in just defining the differences between LANs, MANs and WANs, pinning down the components that make up a network is harder still. This results primarily from the numerous possibilities for the configuration of the network...

In its simplest form, a network requires two computers with the hardware (in this case, two LAN interface cards and appropriate cables) and software necessary to communicate with each other. Once you stray a few steps off that path, the complexity begins....

Regardless of the type or size of a network, every computer tied to it must have a network interface card (NIC) installed and the software to operate it. The graphic illustrates a PCI Network Interface Card. There must also be a transmission path (a medium) for data...

Many networks utilize a Client-Server configuration, where a personal computer (PC) or mainframe computer remains on at all times, operates at high speeds, and has a very large storage capacity. These servers can be either Application Servers, File Servers, or a combination of the two...

Servers act as central access points for client workstations. They validate user logons and may hold software programs or files such as computer-assisted drawing (CAD) programs, databases, etc. When the user workstation consists of a simple terminal and not a PC, file servers are necessary...

Terminals are nothing more than a keyboard and monitor (sometimes a printer); they have no storage capacity for programs or data. Many, however, have extensive random access memory (RAM) and read only memory (ROM) as well as microprocessors...

One other network configuration that exists in many locations is known as a peer-to-peer network. In this configuration, there is no central access point; instead, all user workstations contain their own application programs. Data, such as that contained in a database, may be shared...

In this case, the workstation on which the data is stored assigns share-level access to the other workstations on the network. This configuration works quite well for low-volume networking, where each user workstation is capable of performing some of the functions of a server...

In general terms, the cabling between computers on a network is known as the network's topology. While this is from a strictly physical point of view, it is the most commonly held viewpoint today. Topology can, however, be viewed from a physical and a logical vantage point...

While there are variations on theme, LANs normally conform to one of the following physical topologies: Star, Linear Bus, Tree, Ring, or Star-wired Ring. physical refers to the configurations listed which consist of the cables, connectors and other hardware that are required to create one of the configurations. The Star Topology is one of the oldest of the topologies used in networking. The telephone system was its first use. In recent years, it has become the most popular topology for all networks. Each node is directly attached to a center hub...

ETHERNET - Ethernet is a LAN used for connecting computers, printers, workstations, terminals, servers, etc. within the same building or campus. It operates at 10 Mbps over coaxial cable and twisted wire.
DEFINITION

LOCAL TALK - Local Talk is Apple Computer's LAN for linking Macintosh computers and peripherals. LAN hardware is called Local Talk. It is slower than Ethernet and Token Ring. Appletalk is incompatible with any other LAN.
DEFINITION

If no other stations are transmitting data, that is, if the channel is clear, then it begins its transmission of data. All nodes connected to the bus are receivers of that transmission, typically a data packet. Each receiver then determines if the received data packet corresponds to its own address...

If it does, then the data is acted on; if it does not, then the data is simply discarded. No routing or switching is involved, nor is there any transference of messages from one node to another. The overhead and time required to perform these tasks are eliminated with the bus LAN, hence one of its major attractions...
1. Two stations transmit at exactly the sane time...........

Typically, the stations attempting to gain access to the channel at the same time will back off for a random interval of time before attempting to access the channel again. This allows one of the stations to transmit its data while the others listen. Eventually, the traffic on the network subsides, and fewer collisions occur...

The cabling may be coaxial, twisted pair or fiber optic but will have direct influence on which protocol is used. Several different software protocols can be applied to the linear bus, including Ethernet, Fast Ethernet, and Local Talk...

Fast Ethernet is in the form of an Ethernet hub with an internal bus that runs at 100 Mbps which is ten times faster than the original Ethernet. Now, there's an even faster Ethernet called Gigabit Ethernet...

The tree configuration is a modified version of a linear bus. There is still a main trunk, but extending from the trunk there are branches. Each branch has one or more components (PC, printer, etc) attached. The graphic illustrates one possible physical topography for a tree configuration. Tree topographies normally use Ethernet and Fast Ethernet.....

The ring topology, as the name implies, interconnects nodes point-to-point in a closed-loop configuration. A message is transmitted in simplex mode (one direction only) from node to node around the ring until it is received by the original source node...

Each node acts as a repeater, re-transmitting the message to the next node. Each node also shares the responsibility of identifying if the circulating message is addressed to itself or to another node. In either case, the message is eventually received by the destination station and returned to the original source node.....

The source node then verifies that the message circulated around the ring is identical to the message that was originally transmitted. Acknowledgement bits within the message block are typically set by the destination node so that the source node has a way of verifying that the message was in fact received...

IBM's Token Ring architecture has a physical resemblance to a star. Stations are linked together to a central connection point called a MAU (multistation access unit). The MAU acts as the hub of the network and connects up to eight nodes or computers...

They can also be linked together to extend the number of nodes on the network. The interface cable between the computer station and the MAU is called a lobe, and patch cables are used to interconnect MAUs together...

Although the network topology here appears to be a star, a closer look at the internal connections of the MAU reveal that the electrical ring is preserved; data is allowed to pass directly from one node to another without going through the MAU. For these reasons, IBM's Token Ring topology is referred to as a star-wired ring.....

A token or supervisory frame must be received by an attached terminal or workstation before that terminal or workstation can start transmitting. The workstation with the token then transmits and uses the entire bandwidth of whatever communication media the token ring network is using. Operating speeds are 4 Mbps or 16 Mbps.....

If this were the only benefit, it alone would justify the use of wireless. Wireless LANs, however, actually offer many benefits: 1) mobility, 2) flexibility, 3) fast installation, 4) reduced costs, 5) scalability, and 6) security.....

From one perspective, the term wireless LAN is somewhat of a misnomer. Most wireless LANs are, at some point, connected to a wired system. Normally, only the user end is actually wireless, although LANs that span from one building to another commonly have a wireless link between buildings...

LANs provide the workplace with a tremendously efficient means of sending and receiving information from point-to-point or from point-to-multi-point. Most wired LANs conform to standards defined by the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE) under the specifications identified as IEEE 802.3, 802.4 and 802.5.....

Wireless LANs use standards established under IEEE 802.11. IEEE 802.11 provides the operational guidelines and specifications (throughput, frequency range, speed, distance, etc.) to which wireless systems should conform...
Through put, Frequency range, speed, distance, etc.

The standard also provides a contention mechanism that allows nodes to share a common channel and a collision avoidance mechanism to keep transmitted packets from trying to access the system at the same time. IEEE 802.11 defines not only the recommended operating parameters for RF-based systems but also for infrared (IR) systems.....

Telecommunication protocols are a complex assortment of hardware and software rules, requirements, and responsibility assignments. The IEEE standards are based on a protocol stack divided into seven layers with each layer assigned a specific task or set of tasks that must be performed at a specified time during any communication activity.....
Provides for program-to-program communications.
Manages data representation conversions (code conversions).
Establishes and maintains communications channel.
Controls end-to-end integrity of data transmission.
Physically passes data from one node to another.
Manage the placement and removal of data to or from the network.

The seven-layer stack, based on a proposal by the International Standards Organization (ISO) is called the Open System Interconnection (OSI) Reference Model. The graphic illustrates the seven-layer system...

The principles that ISO applied to arrive at the seven layers were: 1) A layer should be created where a different level of abstraction is needed.
2) Each layer should perform a well-defined function.
3) The function of each layer should be chosen with an eye toward defining internationally standardized protocols.
Provides for program-to-program communications.
Manages data representation conversions (code conversions).
Establishes and maintains communications channel.
Controls end-to-end integrity of data transmission.
Physically passes data from one node to another.
4) The layer boundaries should be chosen to minimize the information flow across the interfaces.
5) The number of layers should be large enough that distinct functions need not be thrown together in the same layer out of necessity, and small enough that the architecture does not become unwieldy.

The goal of the layered system is to have each layer with independent standards so that a change in one layer would not affect the others. Due to the variety of IEEE 802.x standards, some variations to the OSI model may occur. They will, nonetheless, closely resemble the seven-layer model...

When LANs are connected together to form a WAN or a MAN, the network requires specialized devices. Aside from providing a physical link between two LANs, they allow for an association of OSI layers between the LANs based upon the make-up of the LANs being connected...

The function of repeaters is to transmit signals from one segment to another without altering the integrity of the signal. Segments cannot be separated by more than 100m: two 50m-transceiver cables separated by the repeater. The network can then be extended beyond 500m by joining segments together...

There are two types of repeaters: the local repeater and the remote repeater. Both types of repeaters serve the function of joining segments. The remote repeater, however, allows the network to be extended to a maximum of 1000m via a fiber-optic link. The repeater performs physical layer operations only...

Bridges are not commonly used in new installations any more but are still found in existing LANs. They normally connect LANs that have identical protocols at the Data Link and Physical layers of the OSI Model (two IEEE 802.3 Ethernet LANs, for example)...

When a bridge receives a packet, it stores the entire packet in memory, checks it for errors, and then transmits it through the correct port. In this way, the ports are isolated. This accommodates connecting similar LANs, such as variations of Ethernet, together. More sophisticated bridges can connect dissimilar LANs.....

Routers are used to interconnect LANs at the network level. When a router receives a packet, it determines if the packet is destined for a network directly connected to it or if it needs to go to a distant network via one or more additional routers...

For directly connected routers, the packet is sent to the appropriate port and transmitted. For distant networks, the packet is transmitted to the appropriate router. Routers utilize the first three layers of the OSI Model...

Gateways are the most sophisticated devices. They operate to interface all seven layers of the OSI Model and provide complete hardware and software translations between entirely different networks. They can also connect a LAN to a host using an entirely different protocol family. This makes them the most useful and flexible interconnection devices available.........................
There are two transmission formats for wireless networks: RF (radio frequency) and IR (infrared). Both systems have their advantages and disadvantages, but presently RF systems are more popular...
Which is not a transmission format used for wireless networks?
Radio frequency (RF) is one of the transmission formats used for wireless networks.
TRY AGAIN!
Infrared (IR) is one of the transmission formats used for wireless networks
TRY AGAIN!

RF systems use two different transmission techniques: either conventional narrowband microwave or spread spectrum. Spread spectrum is the most commonly used. The narrowband microwave is almost exclusively used for transmissions between LANs from one building to another. This is done with a conventional line-of-site dish antenna.....

The LANs themselves normally use spread spectrum. The spread spectrum technique is either frequency hopping or direct sequence. ll in frequency hopping the signal is sent to many different channels over a broad range. The signal only remains at any given channel for a few milliseconds before being redirected to another channel. The channel sequence is based on a binary code.....

Recall in frequency hopping the signal is sent to many different channels over a broad range. The signal only remains at any given channel for a few milliseconds before being redirected to another channel. The channel sequence is based on a binary code.iven channel for a few milliseconds before being redirected to another channel. The channel sequence is based on a binary code.....

Direct sequence systems use a spreading code (a pseudo-random sequence of ones and zeros) to disperse the signal over a large band of frequencies at very low amplitudes. The receiver must be set to use the same sequence in order to decode the signal. Any other spread spectrum signals not using the same code are summarily dismissed by the receiver as noise.....
Which is not a spread spectrum technique used in RF-transmission systems for computer networks?
Direct sequence is a spread spectrum technique used in RF-transmission systems for computer networks.

Frequency hopping is a spread spectrum technique used in RF-transmission systems for computer networks.

The primary benefits of an RF-based LAN are that line-of-sight is not necessary between the hub or backbone and the node. RF will generally pass through walls, people, and other objects without any signal degradation. At the same time, the use of spread spectrum provides a high degree of security due to the code processes and very low signal levels.....

Infrared systems transmit signals using frequencies in the infrared region of the spectrum. This is the same technology used in the remotes for televisions and VCRs. While the systems work well, the individual nodes must have line-of-sight with the transmitter...

Any objects in the path of the transmitter and receiver (including non-solid objects such as smoke, smog and moisture) will degrade or block the transmission. The line-of-sight characteristic of IR-based systems also makes it difficult for administrators to move workstations...

In some cases, when a LAN is in an enclosed area, a method called sun & moon configuration can be established. In this form, the enclosed area must be able to reflect the infrared light off walls and ceilings. This is also known as diffusion, which allows operation of IR transmissions without line-of-sight...

Because infrared transmissions are unable to penetrate walls, ceilings, floors, etc., they have an inherent security benefit, but their primary advantage is that they have the ability to carry a high bandwidth...

One further benefit of an infrared system is that because the intelligence is being transmitted in the form of light, it will not interfere with other radio signals and, therefore, does not require licensing from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)...

Wireless communications has soared due to technological advances in communications coupled with the demands for personal mobility. Personal communications services (PCS) are the most recent wireless technology to explode. Wireless communications includes more than pagers and cell phones...

It also includes wireless speakers and intercoms, cordless telephones capable of being used up to a mile away from the base station, two-way radio systems, palmtop computers and fax machines linked to wireless modems, the global positioning system (GPS), and wireless medical instruments...
The broad range of PCS services include digital cellular

telephony with voice mail, caller ID, e-mail, and alphanumeric two-way paging systems. Competition among service providers and equipment manufacturers will fuel the demand for PCS services along with personal communications satellite services (PCSS). nces in satellite systems and wireless technology will put the cellular phone system in the sky.....

1. Networks are defined as an arrangement of electronic devices designed to communicate with one another. A simple network consists of two computers with network interface cards, appropriate cables, and the software necessary to communicate with each other.

2. LAN stands for Local Area Network and can encompass areas tens of miles wide. LANs are generally privately owned and they operate in the kilobyte range with a very small error rate. LANs normally conform to one of the following physical topologies: star, linear bus, tree, ring, or star-wired ring..
low signal-to-noise ratios (better noise rejection)

3. WAN is a Wide Area Network and, as the name implies, covers a larger geographical area than LANs. They are usually considered public networks and are a service that the user pays for like the Internet. WANS operate in the megabyte range but have a considerably high rate of errors.
4. MAN stands for Metropolitan Area Network and can be thought of as two or more LANS connected together in a geographically restricted area.

5. Open System Interconnection Model is a telecommunications protocol containing seven layers. Each layer is assigned a specific task(s) that must be performed at a specific time during any communications activity.
Provides for program-to-program communications.
Manages data representation conversions (code conversions).
Establishes and maintains communications channel.
Controls end-to-end integrity of data transmission.
Physically passes data from one node to another.
Manage the placement and removal of data to or from the network.

6. The Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE) defined standards that both wired and wireless networks use to operate. They provide operational guidelines and specifications such as throughput, frequency range, speed, distance, etc.
Through put, Frequency range, speed, distance, etc.
7. There are two transmission formats for wireless networks: radio frequency (RF) and infrared (IR). Most infrared LANs require line-of-sight alignment while RF systems do not.
8. Wireless LANs normally use spread spectrum modulation for data transmission. The two methods of spread spectrum used are direct sequence and frequency hopping.
